utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Ekkehard Withopf, and the case manager, Kimberly Fleming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And could we have the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Alexis Demirdjian, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone, the Prosecution, the Defence teams, the accused, and everyone else present in the courtroom. We are going to continue with the hearing that started yesterday, and the cross-examination will proceed today. Could the usher bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Mrso. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence counsel will continue with its cross-examination. They may now take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Mrso.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday we discussed a number of issues, and I would now like to discuss again the role you played in Bugojno. Yesterday you in fact said that towards the end of 1992 or at the beginning of 1993 you were elected as a member of the Bugojno HDZ committee. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were 20 members in that committee; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the deputy president of the committee; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The committee was formed -- well, there were 20 members in the committee, and there was a 7-member presidency in the committee, but I wasn't part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the position that you held enabled you to be informed about the events that unfolded in the territory of the municipality of Bugojno; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When your committee was sitting, the most important issues that you discussed, the ones you were most interested in, were questions that related to defence; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were other issues too. Those weren't the only questions. Social welfare for the inhabitants, the situation, et cetera, et cetera. These were other matters of interest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had information about these issues which you received on a daily basis; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When testifying in the Kordic case, in response to a question put to you by Mr. Nice you said that the information you received was on a daily basis. In fact, you said -- you described what was happening in Bugojno very precisely; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May 1992, the Serbian forces started shelling the town of Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 24th of May was the first time. It was in the afternoon at about 4.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Kupres and Donji Vakuf had been taken, the Serbian forces blocked passage for the Muslims and Croats in Bugojno; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, Bosnia and Herzegovina had already been recognised as a state and had become a member of the United Nations; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mobilisation and a state of war was declared in the country; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you say so, that's probably right. But I didn't really make a note of the dates and I don't remember them either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina, you were probably aware of the fact that at the time the only legitimate structure after the JNA had attacked the country was the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the majority of the Croatian population responded to the call-up for mobilisation and they mobilised into the HVO, and in 1992 the HVO had, on the whole, the same objectives and the same defence lines as the defence for Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Territorial Defence; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the HVO structures didn't recognise the Supreme Command of the -- the Supreme Command of the Territorial Defence, but they recognised the Supreme Command, the headquarters in Grude; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, I don't know. I wasn't part of those structures. I didn't take any decisions. So to be quite frank, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to a question put to you by the Prosecution yesterday, you mentioned certain attempts made in May 1992 to establish a joint command of the HVO and the Bugojno Territorial Defence Staff. They attempted to establish a joint command for the defence of the town; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, although such a decision was taken, it was never implemented and that joint command never functioned; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that it's correct, but I do know, according to the stories that were circulating, that this didn't really function as it should have done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in May -- at the end of May 1992, they started forming parallel bodies of power in Bugojno itself. In addition to the Territorial Defence units, there were HVO units. And then the HVO formed its own security council or Crisis Staff, which was separate; the HVO MUP or of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and so on. Is it correct to say that as of that time they started forming parallel bodies of power?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say, madam. I wasn't included in those processes, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 104th HVO Brigade was formed in Bugojno. Its name was Eugen Kvaternik; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was another one too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later, at the beginning of 1993, a Home Guard Battalion was established; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether its name was the Home Guards Battalion, but yes, there was the 1st Battalion. And I think its name was Tomasevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 104th Battalion was called the Eugen Kvaternik Battalion; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second one that you have just mentioned was formed in February 1993. It was based on the territorial principles and it had about 1.250 members; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time in Bugojno, you could see with the naked eye that units were far better equipped, they had better uniforms, better weapons, than the BH army units which were only being formed at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't have the exact information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if it's not 100 per cent precise, would this assessment be correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't discuss numbers. I wasn't part of that. I didn't have any weapons, I didn't have a uniform, I didn't have anything. I had a work obligation to perform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me now ask you about certain other subjects. Perhaps you know something more about them, given the position that you held. Would it be correct to say that at the time, in the course of 1992, a large number of refugees arrived in Bugojno, mostly Muslim or Bosniak refugees; they arrived from Jajce, Donji Vakuf, Prozor, Kupres, Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These refugees in fact arrived without any possessions, without anything. They didn't have any property of any kind, so to speak. And since the town was surrounded, there was a demographic explosion which gave rise to significant problems, as far as feeding the refugees and finding accommodation for them was concerned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time many refugees moved into abandoned houses, the houses of people who had left Bugojno because of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the exact information, but I have heard about such cases too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The vicinity of the front lines and everything that happened in the course of the war made the population move from the town to places in the republic that were more secure and made them move abroad, to Croatia and to other parts of Europe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Many inhabitants of Bugojno, both Croats and Muslims, and especially mothers and their children, left the town of Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since most of the people who came were Muslims and Bosniaks, the structure of the population in Bugojno, the composition of the population in Bugojno, changed to a significant extent; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is one of the elements that had an influence on increasing the tension between the Bosniak and the Croatian population and between the HVO and the BH army; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your testimony yesterday, you said that when you were arrested and taken through the town people called you an Ustasha, and so on. This is how they insulted you. Perhaps it would be good to clarify who the Ustashas was. That was the army in the course -- that existed when -- in the course of the Second World War, and they fought on the side of Nazi Germany and they didn't recognise Bosnia and Herzegovina as a state and they didn't recognise the Muslims as a people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know much about that ideology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the time, in individual HVO units and in HVO headquarters, you could see various sorts of insignia that reminded one of that period; there were fascist signs, there were portraits of Ante Pavelic, the head of the independent state of Croatia. And the brigade itself had the name Eugen Kvaternik. He was a very close -- one of the close associates of Ante Pavelic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would meet people wearing uniforms, but I didn't see these signs when these soldiers appeared in public.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The HVO had its own checkpoints around the town. And leaving the country should also make it possible to go through the territory under HVO control. Is it correct to say that those facts made it necessary to get permission from the HVO if one wanted to leave the town?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know anything about that. When I had to go out on business, I didn't ask for such a permit. It was only towards the end of 1993 that I had to leave and ask for a permit. Sorry, not at the end; it was before the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, is it correct to say that many of your Muslim acquaintances also asked you to intervene on their behalf with the HVO so that they could receive a permit to move around freely?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to move around freely. To leave the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, to leave the town. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On occasion, you succeeded in obtaining this, not because you had the authority to do so but you asked HVO representatives in Bugojno to give them such permits; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And each one of them got such a permit, if they had asked for a permit through me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that this prohibition of movement for the Bosniaks was also used as a way of exerting pressure in order to achieve certain objectives of the HDZ and HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Allow me to explain this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead, briefly.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do we have to ask the Presiding Judge for his permission?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness would like to give a brief explanation concerning these permits for leaving the town, for the Bosniak population.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the Serbs attacked, when Bugojno was surrounded, I publicly said that Bugojno shouldn't be left. As the shelling intensified, the shelling of Bugojno intensified and we were afraid, my position was that permits shouldn't be granted to leave the town, not for anyone. For me, in my opinion, this was Serbian aggression against Bugojno. In spite of all the disagreements, at the time I didn't think that there might be a conflict between the Muslims and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that these permits weren't a manner of exerting pressure on the Bosniaks in order to achieve certain objectives and to make it advantageous for the HVO in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I couldn't get a permit, even though I had to leave on business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now like to show the witness a conclusion from the HVO. The source of the document is the Institute for Investigation for Crimes Against Humanity and the Institute for International Law in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, is this a document of the Croatian Defence Council of Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can see, that is what it says, if that is an authentic document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document prohibits the issuance of travel permits to persons of Muslim nationality.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until an agreement is reached in connection with the economy. What that means, I don't know. What has the war and the economy got to do with one another?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in view of the relevance of this document, which relates to the events linked to Bugojno, I would like to tender this document into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution objects to tendering this document into evidence. Again, the very same issue as yesterday; this document is not of any relevance in respect to the charges of the Third Amended Indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the Defence. You heard the objection on the part of the Prosecution, which submits that this document has no relevance in relation to the charges made against the accused. What is the position of the Defence regarding relevance?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we presented several arguments yesterday. This time we would like to say that this is a document which indicates the systematic attitude adopted in Bugojno and which provides the answer to the question why and when conflicts arose between the army and the HVO in this area. From the standpoint of a commander at a high level of responsibility, then events of this kind are certainly very relevant with respect to any measures that he may take or his knowledge as to what was going on in the area. In view of the fact that my client is not charged with any personal offence, documents of this kind can be relevant from the standpoint of his Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will rule on this document after the break. We will have time to see whether it will be admitted or not, so we will deliberate during the break, unless the Prosecution wishes to speak again. Yes, I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, very briefly. This document has been issued the 4th of October, 1992, which is clearly a time frame outside the time frame of the present indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will deliberate on it in a moment. Please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you have testified, in 1993 these tensions led to small and larger conflicts in the town and at checkpoints between the army and the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I was told and as far as I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Additionally, the constant armed conflict between the army and the HVO, in the immediate vicinity and further beyond, had a negative repercussions on the events in Bugojno. That is, the permanent conflicts first at the end of 1992 in Prozor; then in January and onwards in Gornji Vakuf, which is only 18 kilometres from Bugojno; then conflicts in Novi Travnik and Travnik were events which additionally contributed to tensions between the army and the HVO in Bugojno. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I must take a drink. Towards the end of your testimony yesterday, you said that on the 8th of April, 1993 you attended a meeting between presidents and vice-presidents of municipal HVOs, presidents and secretaries of the municipal boards of the HVO for Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the military commanders of the 3rd Operative Zone of the HVO. That was held in Travnik. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the titles are quite right. I was a delegate on behalf of the municipal HDZ of Bugojno. I was not the secretary or the president or the vice-president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If in the minutes, dated the 8th of April, 1993, "Strictly Confidential," number 04-03/93," it is indicated that you attended as vice-president of the HDZ for Bugojno, then that is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is incorrect. I can provide appropriate documents in support of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never asked for those minutes to be corrected, though according to those minutes, you were the vice-president of the HDZ for Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw those minutes, madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that at that meeting also present were Colonel Dario Kordic, the vice-president of the HDZ and the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that he was present. I didn't know what his duties were. I hear that now from you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also present were the presidents and vice-presidents of Herceg-Bosna and representatives from all other areas, and this was an occasion for you to be introduced to various and numerous representatives of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that that is quite correct. You say that there were representatives. I know that Mr. Blaskic was there, Mr. Kordic, Mr. Ignac Kostroman, Ivo Lozancic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ante Valenta?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ante Valenta; you're quite right. But I personally -- believe me -- didn't know what their positions or duties were. I just knew them by first and last names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that at that meeting matters were reviewed linked to the functioning of the HVO authorities and instructions given for future work?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that there was a debate on the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan, and on that basis authorities were to be established. And I think Vlado Soljic was appointed governor or whatever the position was for the canton, anyway a territorial unit. I'm not quite sure what it was called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that at that time numerous conclusions were adopted regarding the establishment of HVO authority in all areas of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that I never saw those minutes to this day. I'm not familiar with the conclusions. I personally took the floor to the effect that the situation was not good, that some sort of authority needed to be formed as soon as possible, because we were already noticing tensions in Bugojno. I said then that people should not be allowed to leave because it was quite obvious that under such heavy shelling something was in the offing. And speaking to people from the party and representatives of the army on the Croatian side, I was not satisfied with their solutions. And I objected and criticised them for giving them permission to leave Bugojno when we expected the Serbs to enter Bugojno in a matter of days. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you said that the HDZ should intensify its activities in all areas?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, I said that I am not familiar with the conclusions, nor have I ever seen them, and I don't remember them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that it was concluded that the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina should be proclaimed unlawful throughout the territory, as the TO had already been proclaimed unlawful?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim I am not aware of those conclusions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you attended that meeting to the end.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that shortly or immediately after that meeting, that is, the 8th of April, 1993, the HVO of Bugojno at a session held on the 10th of April, 1993, adopted a decision in connection with the Muslim leadership and a decision prohibiting issuing permits to Muslims to leave the town and also a decision to block Muslim accounts in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a deputy at the time. I did not have a part in that, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though you were present at the meeting held on the 8th of April, you don't know how those conclusions were implemented in Bugojno only two days later?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. And the document you've shown me is one I'm seeing for the first time in my life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you to look at another document, perhaps again for the first time in your life. And it may refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would like the minutes on the meeting of the Bugojno HVO to be shown to the witness. This document also originates from the archives of the Institute for the Investigation of Crimes Against Humanity and International Law, based in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I am asking the Defence, who is producing this document, that this document, which is the minutes of a meeting that was held on the 10th of April, 1993, in the former post office building, chaired by Mr. Soljic had participants, that is, Raguz, Lucic, Krajinovic, Dragun, Klepic, Milosevic [as interpreted], and Pavlovic; and the witness is not listed. You want to ask the witness on a meeting which he did not attend. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I know that he didn't attend, because I'm familiar with the contents of the minutes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Thank you for drawing my attention to it. I'm asking the witness whether he's familiar with the decisions of that meeting. Because in those days he was politically active in the HDZ. And let me immediately say that it is relevant, because I wish to tender this document into evidence. The Defence finds that it is relevant due to the simple fact that through other questions we wish to show that paragraph 26 of the indictment is incorrect because in it the Prosecutor claims that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the summer of 1993 carried out large-scale attacks on certain places, among which Bugojno is listed. And all these documents show what was the cause of the conflict and how that conflict broke out. Therefore, the background of the indictment is something that the Defence is challenging as well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would appreciate a copy of the document, if Defence counsel is going to be referring to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, first for the very reason you, Mr. President, already drew the attention of Defence counsel of - namely, due to the fact that the witness wasn't present at this particular meeting - the Prosecution objects to use this document and to tender it into evidence and to even ask questions to the witness in respect to this document. And, number two, again, the contents of this document appear to be not relevant in respect to the Third Amended Indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have not answered the other point that was raised by the Defence, and that is they explicitly referred to the indictment with regard to the attacks that took place, the Defence believing that -- contrary to what is indicated in the indictment, by this document the Defence is proving the opposite to what it states. And that is why she wants to ask this witness questions and to tender this document into evidence, which according to the Defence contradicts certain parts of the indictment. What would be your response to that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in paragraph 26 of the indictment, the Prosecution is referring to the fact that in early summer 1993 ABiH units conducted a number of attacks including within the area of the municipality of Bugojno. It doesn't say anything to the extent which army actually caused the hostilities, and that's what I understand is Defence trying to prove via this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence is going to put a question to the witness regarding the contents of the document and we will see in a moment whether it should be admitted or not. So, Mrs. Residovic, I give you the floor to put your question to the witness about the document you have produced.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, my question is: In the capacity that you had at the time in the HDZ in Bugojno, two days after the conclusions were adopted in Travnik were you aware of the conclusions adopted by the Bugojno HVO prohibiting freedom of movement for the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, madam. As has been said, I did not take part; I was not present; and I said yesterday that the board as such was not working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Though you were not working, not just you but other members of the party and its leadership were invited and did attend this large meeting in Travnik, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I said that the municipal board of Bugojno Municipality was not working at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let us move on to another topic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President. Mr. President, the Prosecution objects against this line of questioning. It is obvious from the document and it is confirmed by the witness that he wasn't at this meeting. Therefore, any additional questions in relation to that meeting can't be put to the witness by the Defence. The witness is not in a position to testify anything about this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness, when answering the Prosecution's question, discussed many subjects that he found out about subsequently. He even talked about matters that he had found out about through the media. So the witness has political function, and this might enable him to be aware of the answers. My question was whether he found out anything about this. The witness said that he hadn't found anything about this. Won't ask any more question, but the fact that he wasn't present at the meeting can't be a reason to prevent me from asking additional questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, ask him whether he was familiar with the contents of the document and with the conclusions that it contains. One of them concerns Bugojno Radio, so there was media coverage at the site. I don't know whether he listened to the radio. If he's telling us that he doesn't know anything about this, we'll draw the relevant conclusions. Mrs. Residovic, please proceed with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, you heard Mr. President's suggestion. Did you find out about any other conclusions that were adopted at that HVO meeting; for example, the one that concerns the television and then the one concerning celebrations.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen the document. This wasn't published anywhere. It didn't appear in newspapers of any kind. As to whether it was on the radio, I don't know. Very often the electricity was cut off. Some people were able to listen to the radio; others weren't. This is the first time I have heard about this and the first time I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suggest this be admitted into evidence, because it is a relevant document. The Trial Chamber shall then adopt a decision and I will move on to another subject now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence wants to move on to another subject. We said that we would deliberate in a minute. Is there anything else you would like to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very briefly. Irrespective of the relevance or the non-relevance of the document, in any event Defence can't tender this document into evidence, a document about a meeting the witness didn't attend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, would it be correct to say that the relationships between the army and the HVO in Bugojno became especially tense in May 1993, which is when armed conflicts occurred too?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I couldn't tell you the exact time or date, but that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that on the 9th of May,1993 - that is to say, after these meetings - the HVO captured 38 members of the BH army at the HVO checkpoint in Humac?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I think that that isn't true, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that on the 9th of May, the HVO in Pavic Polje captured another nine -- another seven members of the BH army. They released five of them and two of them were tortured, and after having been tortured they were killed and thrown into the Vrbas River; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct do say that between the 9th and 10th of May they captured more HVO members and in response the army captured 20 HVO members?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that they captured BH army members and in response they captured HVO members?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. First of all, in transcript, page 21, line 7, the witness's response does not appear. So perhaps it would be good to have that response translated. I asked him about the capturing of these BH army members, and I think that the witness said that he hadn't heard about that. But could the witness please answer the question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that seven BH army members were taken prisoner, five were released, and two were killed?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but when? At what time and what was the date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was on the 9th of May, 1993 in Pavic Polje.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Pavic Polje isn't part of Bugojno municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bugojno HVO captured them.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution again objects against this line of questioning. There is no relevance of these questions in respect to the charges in the Third Amended Indictment against the two accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to this comment, the Trial Chamber notes, when looking at paragraph 26 in the indictment in English, the following is stated: "In 1993, until the 18th of March, 1994 --" but I have the French translation. But I'm look at the English version; it says that "The BH army participated in an armed conflict with the HVO." So the period concerned is 1993 until the 18th of March, 1994. And it says in particular "In April 1993." The question you have asked concerns May 1993; isn't that correct? So in fact Defence counsel is asking a question about an event that took place on the 9th of May, 1993; the indictment states that "In 1993 until the 18th of March, 1994, there was a conflict between the BH army and the HVO," the Croatian Defence Council. So these are the relevant elements. You may take the floor. The question is whether the Defence, in the course of its cross-examination, can ask a question about an event that took place in May 1993. Isn't that what's at stake?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, there's a difference between paragraph 26 of the indictment and the line of questioning -- questions Defence is asking. Number one, the witness just said that Pavic Polje isn't part of Bugojno municipality. So the question related to this area isn't incorporated in the present indictment. And, number two, Defence is not asking questions in relation to military attacks. Defence is asking questions in relation to crimes allegedly committed by HVO troops; that's a very different issue. The scope of the indictment certainly doesn't address any crimes committed or allegedly committed by the HVO in an area outside the municipality of Bugojno, and this is the respective municipality we are referring to at this point in time of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. With regard to this conflict between the Prosecution and the Defence, the Trial Chamber notes that the witness says that he knows nothing about the question you put to him. So it's really not necessary to continue, since he says "I don't know." But I'll turn to the witness now. Were you familiar with what happened on the 9th of May, 1993? This is something that concerns the person mentioned -- the place mentioned, Pavic Polje. Were you familiar with this event? Witness, could you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, believe me, they've mentioned Pavic Polje. That's a village which belongs to the municipality of Donji Vakuf. I couldn't say that I heard about that incident, because I haven't. I really know nothing about such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, allow me to move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that as a countermeasure against that event, the BH army in the night between the 9th and 10th of May captured a group of 20 HVO members?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, madam, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that because of the tension that was very high at the beginning of May and caused an armed conflict to break out, the HVO headquarters and the army command made efforts to calm the situation down?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that. And well, if that's the period concerned, they discussed the possibility of establishing a joint TO, a Territorial Defence. But later I heard -- but I only heard about this, because I wasn't a direct participant. They said that they couldn't come to an agreement because of leadership, because of various things. They talked about separating the lines between the Serbs, and they said that they couldn't establish joint lines. I heard about this. We discussed this matter among ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that as a result of those agreements all the people captured were released, both those belonging to the HVO and those belonging to the army?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I wasn't involved in this. I didn't have any contact with these people, because there was some sort of a quarrel. They wouldn't recognise our party -- the party. We wouldn't recognise them, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Mrso. Would bit correct to say that at the exit of Bugojno towards Gornji Vakuf, a few kilometres away there is the village of Vrbanja, which at the time had about 600 inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Vrbanja. But as to how many inhabitants it had, I don't know. I would have to check this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 17th of July, 1993 at the crossroads towards the village Kandija in the village of Vrbanja the HVO established a checkpoint where they started arresting Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think that's correct. I think the opposite happened. There was some sort of a paramilitary unit there. That's at least what people would say, the locals. Dursum was in charge of it; that was his nickname. I know that person well. And Ismet Hadzibegovic was involved. But I couldn't go to that checkpoint, and I don't have any direct information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know that as a reaction to the first fact mentioned -- that you are not aware of, but you are aware of it -- you said that members of the army and the MUP, who were local inhabitants of Vrbanja, in front of the HVO checkpoint towards Bugojno they established their own checkpoint, about 500 metres before it?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said I don't know about either of the checkpoints. I know that they later told me that this Dursum's formation was active, but I don't know about either of the two checkpoints. At the time, I couldn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution again - again - objects against this line of questioning. The witness answered the last question by my learned colleague with "no." And my learned colleague said, "So you know that as a reaction to the first fact mentioned, that you are not aware of, but you are aware of it." I really don't know what this line of questioning will lead to. The witness said he doesn't know, and it's not up to the Defence to interpret this answer, a clear answer, in the exact opposite direction. The Prosecution strongly opposes such a line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. Perhaps there was a translation error. I didn't say that the witness knew about this. I said that he confirmed that he didn't know that the HVO had established that checkpoint. But I asked him whether he knew that in -- as a reaction the army established a checkpoint 500 metres below in the direction of Bugojno. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I said I didn't know. I said that I only heard later on that there was some sort of formation. Dursum was at its head and Ismet Durkovic [as interpreted]. I heard that they were active up there but in what sense, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that that army checkpoint on the 17th of July there was a conflict --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Before we continue, the question you are asking is to know whether he knows that there was a checkpoint. He said no. Witness, you with respect aware of the fact that 500 metres below the city there was a checkpoint? Were you aware of this fact or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I live in the centre of the town. That's about 3 kilometres from the town. I wasn't even able to approach that place, so that's why I'm saying that I wasn't aware of the existence of either of the two checkpoints and I wasn't aware of who had checkpoints up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The question is -- the answer is clear. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that at the checkpoint outside the town, in front of Vrbanja village, there was a conflict between the army and HVO members when members of the army killed an HVO member, Miroslav Telenta [as interpreted] in that conflict? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard that in Vrbanja these two or three young men went for a swim. They were returning, and they were attacked in Vrbanja by Dursum's troops and killed them. That's what we heard in the town. Whether it was a checkpoint there or not -- nothing was said about a checkpoint. They said that that formation attacked them and that they had killed one or two of them. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, is it correct to say that at that time in order to investigate that case the BH Ministry of the Interior and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna MUP formed a joint, mixed patrol consisting of four MUP BH members and four MUP members from the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in order to go to the site to determine what the reasons were for the murder of Mr. Talibir [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that. -- I apologise, but he's not called Telenta, he's called Talenta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were present at the funeral of Mr. Talenta?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you said that at any time, that would have been misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended the funeral of someone else from Glavica. It was in the village of Kula. It was in the cemetery of Glavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was on Saturday, the 17th of July -- not the 18th, the 17th.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, are you aware of the fact that this mixed patrol was attacked by the HVO and that four of the members of BH MUP were killed -- three out of the four were killed and one managed to save himself? Are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What is the new objection that the Prosecution wants to raise? Since this question concerns events that took place in the vicinity of Bugojno, whereas the witness did have certain political responsibilities and may have been informed of certain facts; for example, the composition of the mixed patrol. That's the purpose of the question. That's the sense of the question. What does the Prosecution want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the witness answered the first question in that respect very clearly "I don't know about that," meaning the mixed patrol. That excludes any further questions about the context and about what happened in the context of this mixed patrol. The witness doesn't know, and he said it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my additional question wasn't about the mixed patrols but about the killing of three members of the MUP, a day before the event that the Prosecution claims was provoked by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; that is, that the army attacked Bugojno. We are talking about the hours that preceded that event, which I believe are highly relevant from the standpoint of establishment of the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I address the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do. You can remain seated. You don't have to tire yourself by getting up. I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please do not misunderstand me. I wish to assist the lady and you. At the time when the conflict had almost broken out, our movements were limited. There were days when I didn't dare leave my own house, I didn't dare walk along my own street. Because people were afraid of attacks. People were beaten up, taken away. So many things that perhaps I should have known and appears to you that I should have known I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The witness has explained that if he didn't know things, it was because of the prevalent situation at the time. Please move on to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. As the witness answered many questions on the basis of what he learnt subsequently, then if he didn't know about it on the 17th he may have learnt about it later on. And that is why I'm asking these questions which are relevant for the events in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, is it true that on that same date, that is, between the 17th and the 18th, the HVO attacked the village of Vrbanja, that they arrested 45 inhabitants on that occasion, and that during that attack 54 Bosniak civilians were killed and the village totally destroyed and burnt to the ground? Did you know about that then, or did you learn about it later?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that I couldn't learn about it at the time because I never left my house. I did learn about it later, towards the end of 1993. And as a local citizen of Bugojno I wish to declare that the casualties were exaggerated and that it wasn't so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that through this attack on Vrbanja the casualties of which are the figures I gave, or which you may correct me, were the immediate cause for the escalation of combat to the whole town of Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I couldn't know about that. It was only later, after the attack of the Muslim army on Bugojno - call them what you will - I learnt about these things, and that is at least how things were explained to me; that is, when the Croats started withdrawing, it was the people from Vrbanja that attacked them heavily. This is all on the basis of stories and rumours. I didn't learn anything about any actual actors of those events to be able to claim one way or another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Mrso, we will now move on to the events that occurred when you were arrested and detained. You said that it was your neighbour Reuf who insisted after some bullets had already been fired at your house that you had decided to spend some time with him.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When he came for the second time, he persuaded me. "It would be better for you to come because someone may come and take you away or kill you," et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, you had in your home your own weapons, an automatic rifle and a pistol.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. I never had an automatic rifle or a pistol. Reuf left me his. He said, "Let it be at hand." And I said I didn't even know how to handle it. And he said, "Never mind. Let them see you have one and then they'll get scared."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you told the investigator of The Hague Tribunal something else, then that was not the truth; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I said the same thing to the investigator, because that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm addressing the Defence, because I don't have the written statement. Are you challenging what he said to the investigator regarding the weapons? He has just explained what he had; it was his neighbour who gave it to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said in line 14 what you told the investigator was not the truth. Is that -- if you're asking him this question, which is in the affirmative, that is, to raise a contradiction in relation to what he told the investigator. I don't have that statement. Perhaps the Chamber should have a copy. Because, of course, we need to evaluate the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will come back to that. My colleague is helping me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that Mr. Bourgon is going to find the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until my colleague finds the proper place, I will move on and I'll come back to this question in a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already said that you spent the night at your friend Reuf's house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the morning, you saw some persons in uniform entering your house --

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we heard the noise, and then we saw them. And the shooting, and two grenades went off in my yard. We heard that, and then we started looking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on that occasion, you didn't see the insignia worn by those men regarding their military affiliation.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just saw that they were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. They're trying to help me, but obviously I'll have to find the spot myself, because there are quite a number of pages of this statement. And I apologise for not noting down the relevant passage because I didn't expect the witness to deny this fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we could do is to have the break now, which would allow you to find the relevant paragraph. It is 3.30. We'll have a 25-minute break, as we are having what we call a technical break. And we will resume at five to 4.00. And then we will also be able to rule regarding those two documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for assisting me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed with a few minutes' delay, because as you know, we had to deliberate on those two documents. We are rendering our decision orally, as follows: The Chamber, informed of the tendering into evidence exhibits produced within the framework of the cross-examination of Witness Mrso, the Chamber is of the opinion that it would be appropriate to admit those evidence -- those documents and to have them marked for identification. The Chamber considers these documents not to be admissible at present in this case as evidence. The witness, having clearly indicated through his replies to questions put to him that he did not know those documents and that he was not aware of their content, and therefore, he did not -- and furthermore, he did not attend the meeting that was held on the 4th of October, 1992; and that also he had no knowledge of the substance of that meeting through other sources. Nonetheless, within the framework of a political, historical, and military context of a conflict, the Chamber is of the opinion that these documents could subsequently be tendered if other testimony or other evidence should justify such an admission. At present we have therefore decided to have those documents marked for identification only. In more general terms, the Chamber wishes to remind the parties - the parties in the plural - that within the framework of the cross-examination envisaged by Rule 90(H) of the Rules of Evidence and Procedure, the party which is doing the cross-examination can put all questions that contribute to its case and that are related to its case. The Chamber also wishes to underline that several provisions of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence refer to the political, military, and historical context. This applies also to Rule 92 bis. Similarly, all the judgements of this Tribunal relating to charges refer explicitly and in a detailed manner to the political, military, and historical context. Under those conditions, the Chamber authorises this type of question on condition that the party cross-examining previously inform the Chamber on the aim pursued through these questions and that, in that connection, a decision that was recently brought by this same Chamber, a written decision regarding the scope of the cross-examination has regulated this matter definitively. I invite both parties to re-read that ruling, which allows all questions linked to the context in the cross-examination on condition that the Chamber is informed in a prior manner of the aim of those questions. To conclude, the Chamber invites the Defence, when putting this type of question which may have a certain degree of importance, to take the time when putting such a question to put it slowly so that the witness may think it over and take time himself before answering it. Because otherwise, a question put very quickly, which is sometimes extremely complex can make the witness answer quickly yes or no without himself realising the importance of the question and its impact. Therefore, if a question is important, put it slowly, distinctly, and clearly so that the witness may answer it. That's what I did in explaining our oral decision, which we have just rendered regarding those two documents. As those two documents have been marked -- will be admitted and marked for identification, I would like to ask the registrar to give us a provisional number for the identification of those documents. We have the documents in B/C/S with an English translation. So, Mr. Registrar, give us, please, the numbers for these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the B/C/S version of the record will get the exhibit number DH26; and the English translation of the record will get the exhibit number DH26/E. The conclusion in the B/C/S version will get the exhibit number DH27; and the English translation of the conclusion will get the exhibit number DH27/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Everyone has taken note of the fact that these documents have been marked for identification with the numbers that have just been indicated. I now give the floor again to the Defence to continue their cross-examination. And I would like to ask them once again, if a question is important to put it slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I'd like to go back to the question that I think I am able to ask the witness now. It has to do with the question put to the witness as to whether it was correct to say that he had an automatic rifle and a pistol. And the witness said that he didn't have such weapons, and he said how he obtained those weapons. This is why I would like the usher to show the witness his statement in B/C/S and English that he has signed. And at the same time, I'd like to provide the Trial Chamber with a copy of the decision. I would -- not the decision; I apologise, the statement. And I would also like to say that I won't be tendering this statement into evidence but I will be using it as a basis for my cross-examination. I would also like to inform you that for the purpose of making it easier to translate the relevant sections, we have provided a copy of this document to the interpreters. We did this during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, to make sure that you don't lose the process of the cross-examination, the Defence is providing you with a statement that you have signed. It is in your own language and it has been translated into English on the basis of this written statement taken on the 10th of June, 2000, the 11th of June, the 1st of July, 2000, the 14th of September and the 15th of September, 2000, by an investigator from the OTP. The name is indicated; you were assisted by an interpreter, in fact, there were two interpreters. And the Defence is going to ask you some questions about your written statement. Please try to answer the questions put to you as fully as possible. The Defence may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, would you please have a look at the page. The number is 03004128. That is the Prosecution's number. At the top you have the number 03004128. Would it be correct to say that in the paragraph that starts with the words "at about 4.00 --"

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. It's page 4 in the English version and it's the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, would bit correct to say that on this page it says: "At about 4.00 a.m. the next morning I was woken by someone pounding on my front door. I asked who it was and a voice shouted at me to open up. I refused. Then whoever was outside opened fire. He shot through the windows at the front of my house. I threw myself on the floor. Nothing happened. I got my automatic rifle and waited." Is that what it states here?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please would you now have a look at the paragraph that starts with the words "I decided to go to Reuf's house." In the English version, it is on page 4 [as said] paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page 5, paragraph 4. I apologise. That's the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, does it say: "I decided to go to Reuf's house. He also agreed to hide both my gun and the uniform I owned in his home. I stayed overnight"? Is that what it states?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that when Reuf came to see me on the second occasion, he left his rifle with me. That has to do with the second paragraph. And then I heard someone calling out to me. Reuf then suggested that if I didn't want to go, I should leave the rifle and if someone came, at least that person would be frightened. When we reached his house, I said that he should hide his uniform and the rifle, because if they were searching his house they would claim that it was mine. And with regard to that matter, I pointed out to the Trial Chamber that I always asked the investigator to leave me a copy, a record. They said that the Rules were such that I couldn't be provided with such a copy. And I think that at one point I even intervened and requested that a paragraph be amended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, at the end of the English version, it says that you had requested a statement. This was noted on the 15th of September, 2000. So my question to you is whether what you have testified before this Chamber today and what you stated to Tom Parker - and that is obtained in the paragraphs I have read out - are there differences? Are there discrepancies?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm claiming that I didn't have a rifle. I don't know how to use a rifle. I didn't even believe that it was necessary for me to have one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can keep that statement. Perhaps we'll check some other items. Differing statements were given. The one you gave to the investigator and the statement you have made before the Trial Chamber are not identical. According to your testimony, after these persons whose insignia that you did not notice, after they had left, some people started taking things out of your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that on the following day, on the 21st of July, you went to the house to see what the situation was like? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw that certain items were missing, but you didn't report this to any of the authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no one I could report this to. I couldn't leave the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless you told the soldiers who came to say that shots had been fired from your house, you told them that certain things had gone missing and they attempted to get some of your property back; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 22nd of July, soldiers appeared again and they wanted to search the house. Their explanation was that they were looking for weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, they didn't find any weapons because the weapon was in Reuf's house.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That weapon didn't even exist because the people who came to search the house before didn't find any weapons either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that event, according to your testimony, you were taken to Adolf Tomas's house, which is where some of your fellow Croats were too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent the night there, and on the following day during the day you went to visit your house again; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 24th of July, 1993, you were moved with two other men to that garage; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were released on the 5th of August, 1993. So you spent a total of 11 days in detention; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak up when answering questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When -- during that period, you were in the garage for one night; in the convent, which wasn't a convent for many years before the war. It was a school and a Marxist Centre; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was always called a convent by the locals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You spent five days there, until Friday, the 30th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were then moved to the grammar school. And on Sunday, on the 1st of August, you were moved to the primary school, the Vojin Aleksic [as interpreted] Primary School.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sports hall in the Vojin Aleksic [as interpreted] Primary School.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were released there on the 5th of August.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't in any way maltreated in any of these places, physically maltreated; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, you also said that after four days in the Marxist Centre or, rather, in the convent you were visited by a humanitarian organisation: Vukadin, Dr. Zlatko Strujic, Hrvoje Lucic, and Fra Bruno Batinic and Sister Pavka were in that delegation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it was a humanitarian organisation. I said there were representatives of some international organisation, but I didn't know about it. That's what I think I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in these detention facilities, you said that other people were brought in who had recently been captured. And you said that HVO members were brought in.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember mentioning the HVO. But I said on the following day, on Monday, they put in Niko Dzaja, who had been beaten and people looked at him, wanted to ask him about something. I said, "Leave him alone. Let him come to and then ask him questions."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period, you found out from some of the detainees that all the HVO strongholds were already in the -- in BH army hands but that the resistance in Titovo villa lasted the longest and came under the control of the army on the 27th of August, 1993; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So throughout this period, from the 18th of August up until the 27th of August, in the town and its surroundings, there was intense fighting between the army and the HVO and at that time the town was shelled on multiple occasions.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was in detention, so I wasn't really a participant in these events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mrso, would it be correct to say that before the war Bugojno didn't have a penal facility or a large prison?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I don't know. Maybe it was in the police station or in some other building, but I really don't know whether such facilities existed. In fact, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I say that there was only the municipal court in Bugojno where they tried misdemeanours, would you agree with me? They only tried minor offences there; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I'd agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For serious crimes, people would be sent to the high court in Zenica; isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of the questions put to you by the Prosecution, you said on several occasions that you were only a member of the HDZ committee and that you didn't know much about the structure of the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly, you didn't know anything about the structure of the army, and you answered a question of mine and said that you didn't even know when the BH army received this name.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, in the course of the fighting from the 18th up until the time of your arrest, you had no idea as to the units participating in the fighting in the town.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I saw the inscription "MOS," but as to who they belonged to, what sort of formation they were, I knew nothing about that; I knew nothing about those structures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't even know who commanded those units, and you don't know who they were subordinated to at the time.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you didn't even know who took the decision about the detainees and about where they should be accommodated.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't even know who was in charge for each individual facility in which you spent the period with regard to which you have testified before this Trial Chamber; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got out, when you were released, according to your testimony it wasn't until December that you first met the commander of the 307th Brigade, Tahir Granic, but not even then - because many refused to accept responsibility for the prisons - not even then were you able to know who was responsible for the prisons; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your testimony, you most frequently turned to the president of the War Presidency in Bugojno because you knew that he was in a position to solve the problems that you had told him about.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You became persuaded of this because on the whole he was able to do many of the things that you asked him to do and he did do these things.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you say he did many things, I don't know what you mean. But I don't think that he did many of the things that I had requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, I he was in a position to do some of the things that you had requested.

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as the president of the War Presidency, it's quite clear that he was in a position to do certain things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to remind you again of your statement which you gave to the investigator from the OTP, and it has to do with the knowledge you had about the units that you saw in the town; that is to say, about the units in charge of these prisons. Please first have a look at page 5, the paragraph that begins with the words "Late in the afternoon on the 18th of July." That's in the B/C/S version. And on the English version --

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page is that? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The number is 03004128. That's the Prosecution number. Can you see it? Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: IVO MRSO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So: "In the late afternoon, on the 18th of July, I was at home in the Terzici neighbourhood of Bugojno when I heard a commotion in the street.
